To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oseltamiviresistant influenza A/H1NI viruses in 2005-2009 were associated with reassortment and mutation, and the specific mutation (H275Y) conferring to antiretroviral resistance was acquired in a hitches-hiking mechanism.

the oseltamivirus resistant viruses emerged through intra-subtype 5+4 reassortant virus in 2007–08 and the dominant variant, 2B1 virus, in 2008–09 acquired additional mutations to cause the 2008-09 influenza epidemic in Taiwan.
reassortment and multiple mutations were associated with the emergence and spread of oseltamir-resistance influenza viruses in Taiwan.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular epidemiology of oseltamavir-resistant influenza A/HN1 viruses and provides important information for understanding of the mechanisms of emergence and spread of influenza viruses and for development of effective strategies against the pandemic influenza.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the emergence of oseltamivar-resistant influenza A/HIN1 viruses in Taiwan.
the genetic diversity of influenza A/H1NI viruses in a specific region and the mechanisms responsible for the emergence and spread of resistant viruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H275Y substitution was not the primary driver for emergence and spread but was a hitch-hiker in the evolutionary processes of oseltamivirus-resistant influenza A/HIN1 viruses.

reassortment and mutation, both of which are the two important mechanisms for influenza virus evolution, were involved in the emergence and spread of oseltamir-resistant seasonal influenza A/H3N2 viruses in Taiwan.
the emergence of the resistant virus was due to the reassortment and the specific mutation H275Y was a hitch-hiking event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reassortant viruses with H275Y in NA were more virulent and more easily to spread, and the H275Y was the major factor for oseltamivirs resistance.
reassortment and mutation are the main factors responsible for the emergence and spread of oseltamavir-resistant viruses in the 2005–09 influenza epidemics in Taiwan.
the emergence and spread of oseltamvir-resistant seasonal influenza A/HN1 viruses in 2005-2009 were associated with the reassortment of 4+4, 5+5 and 3+5 viruses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reassortment and mutation are both important for the emergence of oseltamavir-resistant seasonal influenza A/H3N1 viruses and the H275Y is a hitchhiking mutation.
the H275Y substitution is a common mechanism for the oseltamivirus resistance in seasonal influenza A/HN1 viruses and the resistant viruses are likely to spread worldwide.
the H275Y substitution in NA was acquired in a clade-specific manner.
